rows.howToFix: Recall remedy: Tesla service center replaces accelerator pedal — free. All affected VINs covered. Verify your VIN status via NHTSA recall lookup (24V-302). Owners noticed loose pedal pads via simple feel test.

rows.title: Charge Port Latch Freezes in Cold Weather
rows.howToFix: Use the app's Defrost Car or Controls > Service > Inlet Heater for 10-15 minutes before charging; schedule a departure time so the car preconditions the port. Thaw with warm water in a sealed bag, de-icer, or a hand warmer. If the connector is stuck, use the manual charge-cable release in the trunk. Cars built mid-2020+ have the inlet heater which largely resolves it.

rows.title: Front Lower Lateral Link / Control Arm Bushing Tears (Clunk)
rows.howToFix: Tesla sells the arms only as complete assemblies (not the bushings separately), so the standard repair is replacing the affected lateral link / lower control arm assemblies (front lower link OEM PN family 1044351-00-x). Aftermarket press-in bushings or solid bearings (e.g., MountainPass Performance) are available but require a press. Follow with a four-wheel alignment.

rows.title: Front Upper Control Arm Ball Joint Squeak/Creak
rows.howToFix: Replace the front upper control arm(s); Tesla's fix is the complete FUCA assembly (Tesla PN family 1044321-00-x). Aftermarket ball-joint-only kits (e.g., Unplugged Performance) or camber-adjustable arms exist. Confirm it is the FUCA and not a wheel bearing before replacing; some cars need both. A four-wheel alignment is recommended afterward.

rows.title: Frozen Door Handles in Cold Weather (Can't Enter Car)
rows.howToFix: Tesla advises firm strikes around the handle perimeter ('like knocking on a door') to break the ice, then cycling the handle a few times — NOT prying with tools. Precondition/defrost the car from the app before departure, or open the driver door remotely via the app's Unlatch Door quick control. Preventively apply WD-40/silicone to the pivot pins. If the handle mechanism is damaged, replace the handle assembly.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Premature Inner-Edge Tire Wear (Camber/Toe Alignment)
rows.howToFix: Get a four-wheel alignment and set toe to spec; rotate tires every ~6,000 miles and keep pressures at the door-jamb spec (avoid overinflation). For enthusiasts, camber-adjustable front upper arms / rear camber arms reduce negative camber. Inspect inner edges regularly since wear hides on the inside.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Inspect inner edges regularly since wear hides on the inside.

rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Rearview / Backup Camera Loss (Firmware Recall + Trunk-Lid Coax Wear)
rows.howToFix: For the software cause, install the recall firmware (2023.44.30.7 or later) via OTA — no service visit needed; verify VIN against Tesla's and NHTSA's recall lookup. For the coax/harness wear, Tesla replaces the trunk-lid camera cable/harness. If the screen is otherwise fine and only the camera is black, suspect the harness first.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: verify VIN against Tesla's and NHTSA's recall lookup.

rows.title: Taillight Condensation & Trunk-Lid Water Leak
rows.howToFix: Minor taillight fogging can be cleared with gentle heat (hair dryer) so humid air escapes the vent. For persistent water intrusion, Tesla service reseals the trunk-lid seams / replaces the pinched or under-thick taillight gasket, generally under warranty. Some owners add butyl sealant to the taillight gasket as a DIY fix.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Touchscreen Yellow Border / Yellow Band Around Display
rows.howToFix: Tesla's official remedy is a UV-light fixture applied to the screen for ~2-3 hours at a Service Center (cannot be done by Mobile Service); it is typically free under the basic warranty. The fix does NOT require replacing the MCU or screen. DIY owners have used a 365-370nm UV nail lamp with mixed results. If the border returns or the panel is otherwise failing, the display assembly is replaced.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Vampire / Phantom Battery Drain While Parked
rows.howToFix: Let the car sleep (7-10 min after driving/charging). Set a Home favorite so Sentry auto-disables there; turn off Sentry/Cabin Overheat Protection/Summon Standby when not needed; limit frequent-polling third-party apps; disable 'Keep Accessory Power On.' Persistent abnormal drain that doesn't sleep can indicate a component keeping the car awake — log a service ticket.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Windshield/Cabin Fogging with A/C + Recirculation in Cold
rows.howToFix: Keep climate on Auto (which dehumidifies), turn recirculation OFF in cold weather so moist air is exhausted, and use the defog/defrost button (turns on A/C + max heat + fan) to clear glass quickly. Keep cabin filter fresh and remove wet floor mats/snow that add humidity. If fogging persists with fresh air selected, have the HVAC/heat-pump dehumidification checked.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: If fogging persists with fresh air selected, have the HVAC/heat-pump dehumidification checked.

rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Model 3 / Y 12V Auxiliary Battery Premature Failure
rows.howToFix: Lead-acid 12V replacement $150-$250 part + $100-$200 service-center install. Lithium 12V $200-$300 part. DIY is feasible but disabling HV system safely is critical. Many 2018-2020 Model 3 owners report needing 2-3 replacements before lithium retrofit.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Model 3 / Y Paint Thickness + Chipping
rows.howToFix: PPF (paint protection film) on high-impact areas is the durable fix — $500-$2,500 depending on coverage. Touch-up paint from Tesla or 3rd-party color-matched. Severe issues may warrant repaint of panels ($600-$1,500 per panel at independent body shop).
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Model 3 / Y Phantom Braking on Autopilot
rows.howToFix: Update to latest firmware (FSD beta or production); some specific software versions are notably worse. Configure following distance to max (7). Disable Autopilot on roads where phantom braking is frequent. NHTSA investigation remains active — Tesla has not issued a formal recall as of writing.
rows.dispositionReason: The prescribed remedy is dealer, campaign, recall, or software work.

Verify the car is updated and check VIN against the recall. If assist is already lost/hardware-damaged, the EPAS rack/motor assembly is replaced (out-of-recall cost is far higher).

Tesla covers the 12V under the 4yr/50k basic warranty.

rows.title: Charge Port Door / Latch Actuator Failure
rows.howToFix: Short term, use the manual release lever behind the left rear trunk trim to open the door/release the cable, and warm a frozen port. For persistent failures the charge port actuator/latch or the whole charge port assembly is replaced - a ~30-minute mobile-service job. Keep firmware current, as some latch behaviors are software-mediated.

rows.title: Drive Unit / Battery Coolant Leak (LDU Rotor Seal & Cooling Lines)
rows.howToFix: Pressure-test the cooling system to locate the source. For a leaking LDU rotor seal the drive unit is resealed or replaced (reman units are common); for cracked coolant lines/fittings or a failed thermal valve/heat exchanger those components are replaced and the system is refilled and bled with the specified Tesla coolant. Address low-coolant warnings promptly to avoid thermal derate or pack damage.

Replace a failed latch actuator if the mechanism no longer engages. For 'won't latch' cases confirm whether the VIN falls under a frunk/secondary-latch recall for a free inspection and re-alignment.

rows.howToFix: Get a professional HV diagnostic (SMT/Scan My Tesla data plus Tesla toolbox) to determine whether it is a recoverable isolation/thermal/contactor issue or genuine cell/module degradation. Some cars are fixed with a BMS reset, contactor service, or single-module replacement by an independent EV specialist; others need a remanufactured pack. Out-of-warranty full pack replacement is the worst case and the reason many owners pursue module-level rebuilds.

rows.title: Panoramic Sunroof Water Leak
rows.howToFix: Have a Tesla service center re-adjust the roof closure pressure/settings and reseat or replace the rubber seal; clean and lubricate the roof mechanism per the service procedure. Ensure drain channels are clear. Cars with recurring leaks may need the updated seal or spacer correction. The fixed glass roof (2018+) eliminates the problem.

rows.howToFix: Replace the window regulator assembly (OEM), or install an upgraded billet-aluminum ferrule to cure the root-cause weak point at low cost. Check that the regulator/motor mounting bolts are torqued, since loose bolts accompany some failures. Re-calibrate the window after service.

rows.howToFix: Replace the failed handle assembly with a later-generation unit, or install a paddle-gear/micro-switch rebuild kit (billet or upgraded plastic gear) which addresses the root-cause wear part at far lower cost than a full assembly. Retrofitting the Gen 3.0 handle per the Tesla service bulletin is the most durable fix. If only the microswitch/wire has broken the handle can often be repaired without a new assembly.

Repairs range from replacing a leaking air strut/spring or valve block to a new air suspension compressor. Replace the compressor's air dryer to prevent repeat moisture failures.

Some repairs may be covered under Tesla's suspension goodwill/warranty adjustments.

Address any speed-correlated whine before it worsens.

Cracks and any delamination require full windshield replacement using an OEM panoramic unit and recalibration of the forward camera/ADAS. Document delamination early and pursue warranty/goodwill coverage; a quality PPF or windshield film reduces future chip risk.

rows.title: Phantom Braking on Autopilot / Full Self-Driving
rows.howToFix: Keep the car on the latest firmware, which progressively reduced phantom-braking events. Report recurring events to Tesla so they are logged. Drivers should keep hands on the wheel and be ready to override with the accelerator. No hardware repair is required; the remedy is delivered as over-the-air software updates (free).

rows.title: Sentry Mode and Cabin Overheat Protection Excessive Battery Drain (12V and HV)
rows.howToFix: Update to 2024.38.4 or later (40% drain reduction via FSD-computer motion detection offload; MCU stays asleep until video write). Use 2024.32.6+ behavior that cuts 12V outlets/USB in Sentry. Disable Sentry Mode and Cabin Overheat Protection during long-term parking, or whitelist home/work. Replace the 12V battery if drain persists: 2020-2021 and early 2022 builds are flooded lead-acid; production starting late December 2021 transitioned to a 15.5V Li-ion module — do NOT cross-fit the wrong chemistry.

rows.title: TPMS Warning Light Resets Between Drives, Failing to Warn of Low Tire Pressure (Recall 24V935)
rows.howToFix: Tesla pushed a free over-the-air firmware update (release 2024.38.7, 2024.38.10, 2024.40 or later, excluding 2024.44/2024.44.1) that restores compliant TPMS telltale behavior so the warning persists between drives. No service visit is needed.

rows.title: Autopilot/TACC Phantom Braking on Highway (NHTSA PE22-002, 416k Model 3/Y)
rows.howToFix: Keep firmware current; some owners report improvement on newer FSD builds. If recurrent, disable Autopilot/TACC in problem zones and file a complaint at nhtsa.gov so the open NHTSA investigation has data. No mechanical repair available.

rows.title: Electronic Door Handles Inoperative on Low 12V Voltage — Occupants Trapped (NHTSA Investigation PE25-010)
rows.howToFix: No recall remedy has been issued yet (investigation open as of late 2025). Tesla vehicles have manual interior door release levers; owners and passengers should learn the manual-release location for every door (front doors have an obvious mechanical pull; rear doors on Model Y have a hidden manual release). Keeping the 12V/low-voltage battery healthy and replacing it promptly when it weakens reduces the risk. Owners experiencing a dead 12V condition can use the exterior emergency low-voltage terminals to power the front trunk and access the cabin.

rows.title: Windshield Cracking During Cabin Preconditioning / Defrost in Cold Weather
rows.howToFix: Owners are advised to warm the cabin gradually rather than blasting maximum defrost onto very cold glass, and to clear ice mechanically before applying heat. If a crack appears without an impact point during preconditioning, document it and pursue a warranty/goodwill claim, though approval varies. Windshield replacement is the remedy if the glass cracks.

rows.title: Electronic Power Steering Assist Loss From Overstressed Circuit Board (Recall 25V092 / SB-25-00-004)
rows.howToFix: Tesla issued a free over-the-air software update (2023.38.4 or later) that revises the power-up sequence and current handling to prevent the EPS circuit board from being overstressed. No service-center visit is required; owners simply need to ensure the vehicle is updated. Vehicles that already suffered a hardware failure of the steering board are repaired under warranty.

rows.title: Rearview/Backup Camera Image Loss From Shorted Computer Circuit Board (Recall 25V002 / SB-25-00-001)
rows.howToFix: Tesla released free over-the-air software updates (versions 2024.44.25.3 and 2024.45.25.6 or later) that change the power-up sequence to prevent the circuit board / power components from shorting. Any vehicle whose computer already shorted before the update is given a free replacement computer under warranty.

rows.title: Refreshed (Juniper) Model Y Turn-Signal Stalk Fails to Latch / Cancels Early
rows.howToFix: No official recall or fix. Tesla has adjusted behavior through software in some builds; a firm but quick flick is reported to latch it more reliably. Owners frustrated with the operation can raise a service ticket, though Tesla generally treats this as designed behavior. Aftermarket stalk-feel guides and software updates may improve reliability over time.

rows.title: Battery Pack Contactor Opens Suddenly Causing Loss of Drive Power (Recall 25V690 / SB-25-13-001)
rows.howToFix: This is a hardware defect that cannot be fixed over-the-air. Affected owners must take the vehicle to a Tesla Service Center, where technicians replace the battery pack contactors free of charge under warranty.

rows.title: Heavy-load range collapse — 500-mile rating only on light freight
rows.howToFix: Route-plan around real-world ~1.7-2.0 kWh/mi consumption for heavy/dense freight, not the 500-mi marketing figure. Reserve Semis for sub-300-mi lanes that terminate at a Megacharger, and budget a mid-route 30-min charge for any run over ~350 mi at GCW.

rows.title: Parking brake valve module fails to engage — rollaway risk (NHTSA Recall 23V-205)
rows.howToFix: Free recall fix: Tesla Service replaces Bendix Intellipark Towing Park Brake Module (PVM) part 1124642-00-A with revised part 1124642-00-B that has improved internals preventing air leakage. Affects 35 units produced Nov 30 2022 – Feb 28 2023. Verify Recall 23V-205 / Tesla SB-23-33-001 is closed on the VIN before putting the unit in service.
